summary: Regression testing after cookie-based auth migration + App.js refactor. 11/11 backend pytest tests pass; frontend flows (login, session persistence via cookie, sidebar navigation, Mediwiki search + profile, logout) all work end-to-end. httpOnly cookie is set on login, cleared on logout; no auth tokens in localStorage.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py sets cookie with secure=True and samesite='lax'. This is correct for HTTPS preview but any local http testing will silently drop the cookie. Fine for prod-like preview URL used here.
AlertAcknowledgement.note default 'Acknowledged by supervisor' can be misleading if a DDHS user acknowledges; consider passing role in the default or removing the default.
capture_attendance issues status 200 for both accepted/quarantined and already_synced. Consider 201 for new creates for REST correctness.
Mediwiki initial mount fires search('') and renders zero cards momentarily until response — no loading state; minor UX polish.
Sign-out button in sidebar relies on aria-label='Sign out'; consider a data-testid='sign-out-button' for more resilient tests.
server.py `capture_attendance` is reused inside `/attendance/sync` as a function, which works but couples the HTTP handler to the batch path — cleaner to extract the core logic into a helper.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie-based auth confirmed working. backend_test.py uses requests.Session() to persist ddhs_session cookie. Existing /app/tests/test_platform_validation.py (pydantic model unit tests) still passes. For frontend automation, prefer sidebar selectors '.sidebar nav >> text=<label>' since NavItem renders <div> elements without role=button.
